caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 4448 of 2017.
lawyer:
Md Nurul Amin, Senior Advocate, instructed by Zainul Abed in, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioners. 
Biswajit Debnath, Advocate, instructed by Md Ali Azam, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondent.
parties:
Joad Ali Mondal being dead his legal heirs: 1(a) ) Most. Azirun Nessa and others ---- Petitioners
vs
Arun Chandra Biswas -------- Respondent
case_source: (Prom the judgment and order dated 3-8-2017 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5276 of 1998)
full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman, J: This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 3-8-201.7 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5276 of 1998 making the Rule absolute and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 21-9-1998 passed by the Sub-Ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenaidah in Title Appeal No.41 of 1991 reversing the judgment and decree dated 17-2-1991 passed by the Assistant Judge, Shailkupa, Jhenaidah in Title Suit No.257 of 1985 dismissing the suit.

2. The relevant facts for disposal of- this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal in short, are that the petitioner Nos.1-4 and others as plaintiffs, instituted the Title Suit No.257 of 1985 in the Court of learned Munsif, Shailkupa, Jhenaidah against the respondent for declaration that the decree of Title Suit No.400 of 1983 of the said Court was collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon them stating, inter alia, that the defendant obtained a collusive decree on 15-2-1984 in Title Suit No.400 of 1983 by suppressing process of the Court though all the defendants of the aforesaid suit were alive and, as such, the decree of the aforesaid Title Suit No.400 of 1983 was collusive and not binding upon them.

3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the disputed land was recorded in the name of Surendra Nath and others. Debrani, mother of the defendant is the daughter of Upendra Nath, brother of Surendra Nath who inherited the property of her father. Surendra Nath and others gave settlement of their land on 15th Baishak 1358 BS to Amullay Kumar Biswas, the father of the defendant. Debrani transferred her share to the defendant by two deeds of gift. There was a dwelling house in the portion of Debrani where the defendant's father shifted. After the death of his father, the defendant has been possessing the disputed land. In the Hal record the disputed land was not recorded in the name of defendants as a result he filed the Title Suit No.772 of 1983 in the Court of Jhenaidah which was transferred to Shailkupa and renumbered as Title Suit No.400 of 1983. Summons were duly served upon all the defendants. The plaintiff No.6 of the instant case was not alive at the time of filling the suit and the plaintiff No.1 did not file the suit. The plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the disputed land.

4. The trial Court, after hearing the parties, and considering the facts and circumstances of the case and materials evidence on record dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 17-2-1991.

5. Feeling aggrieved, by the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-2-1991 passed by the trial Court, the plaintiff-appellants prefer-red Title Appeal No.41 of 1991 before the learned District Judge, Jhenaidah and on transferred the appeal was heard by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenaidah who allowed the appeal by the judgment and decree dated 21-9-1998.

6. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree dated 21-9-1998 passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenaidah, the defendant as petitioner preferred Civil Revision No.5276 of 1998 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule.

7. In due course, a Single Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties was pleased to make the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 3-8-2017.

8. Feeling aggrieved, by the impugned judgment and order dated 3-8-2017 passed by the High Court Division the plaintiffs as petitioners filed the instant civil Petition for leave to appeal.

9. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the trial Court as well the appellate Court found that on examination of the return of the summons of the Title Suit No.400 of 1983 it is evident that the process server affixed a copy of the summons at the outside of the door of the house of the defendants and in whose presence the copy was affixed was not mentioned in the report. But the High Court Division overlooked the mandatory provision of law and made the Rule absolute which is erred in law and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He further submits that it is an obligation of the process server to mention in his report the name and address of the person by whom the house in question was identified and in whose presence the copy of summons was affixed. When the service reports were devoid of this essential information, it is unacceptable. In the instant case the process server could not mention the name and address of the person in whose presence the summons were affixed which was proved by the trial Court as well as the appellate Court. The High Court Division without following the mandatory provision of law under Order 5 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure made the Rule absolute and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He also submits that in a case for challenging the ex-parte decree for non service of summons, the important issue is that whether the summons was served upon the defendant. But the trial Court as well as the High Court Division erred in law made the Rule absolute by passing the actual issue and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He next submits that the mandatory provision of law that an ex-parte decree will be set-aside if it is found that there was no service of summons on the defendant. The trial Court as well as the appellate Court held that the summons was not served upon the defendant. In such a situation it is the duty of the High Court Division to set-aside the ex-parte decree and discharge the Rule, but the High Court Division erred in law by making the Rule absolute and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be interfered by this Division for ends of justice. He finally submits that in an ex-parte decree, the Court has to observe the minimum legal requirements in passing the ex-parte judgment and decree. In the instant case the learned Munsif Judge observed that "the case is taken up for ex-parte disposal, PW 1 Arun Chandra Biswas is examined on SA case is proved, CF paid is correct. Hence, it is ordered that the suit be decreed on ex-parte against the defendants without cost. Plaintiffs' title over the suit Land be declared. And it is also declared that the RoR is erroneous and not binding upon the plaintiffs". in the ex-parte judgment, the trial Court is not uttered a single word in respect of possession and also about the documents. This does not at all satisfy the legal requirements, nor is it possible from reading the judgment that the trial Court at all applied judicial mind and, as such, the High Court Division erred in law by making the Rule absolute. Hence, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside.

10. Mr Biswajit Debnath, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He submits that the Court of a meal below reversed the judgment of the trial Court without discussing the evidence on record both oral and documentary occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. Hence, the instant petition may kindly be dismissed. He further submits that non service of process of the Court upon the defendants in Title Suit No.400 of 1983 was not proved by the plaintiffs by necessary and legal witnesses and, as such, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. He also submits that the trial Court after due consideration and discussion of evidence arrived at a correct decision that the plaintiffs had no right, title, interest in the suit land of Title Suit No. 400 of 1983 and therefore, they cannot challenge the decree of the said suit and on the other hand the Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenaidah being final Court of fact reversed the judgment of the trial Court without sifting and discussing the evidence on record and, as such, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. He finally submits that the appellate Court below misconceived the judgment of the trial Court in holding that the trial Court committed error in dismissing the suit since he found that the process of the Court were not served upon the defendants but in fact the trial Court held that though there was some irregularities in serving the summons but since the defendants had no right, title, interest and possession in the disputed land, the decree should not be set-aside. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 39 DLR 339 and, as such, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute.

11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the respective parties. Perused the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and other materials on record.

12. By this civil petition the plaintiffs-appellants challenges the judgment of the Single Judge of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute reversing the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below, the suit was for simple declaration that judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.400 of 1983 is collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon them. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the finding that—

“যাহা হোক উপরের আলোচনা থেকে এই সিদ্ধান্ত উপনীত হওয়া গেল যে, তর্কিত দেং-৪০০/৮৩ নং মোকদ্দমার সমন জারীর ক্ষেত্রে কিছু অনিয়ম দৃষ্ট হলো নালিশী জমিতে বাদীপক্ষের কোন স্বত্ব দখল না থাকায় তর্কিত ডিক্রী রদ রহিত যোগ্য লয়। কাজেই বিচার্য্য বিষয় দুটি বাদী পক্ষের প্রতিকূলে নিষ্পত্তি করা হলো । ৫/৬ নং বিচার্ধ্য বিষয়ঃ উপরোক্ত আলোচনা ও সিদ্ধান্তের আলোকে বলা যায় যে, বাদীপক্ষ তাদের প্রার্থিত প্রতিকার বা অন্য কোন প্রতিকার পেতে হকদার নন। কোর্ট ফি সঠিক । অতএব আদেশ হয় যে, অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে দোতরফা সূত্রে খরচাসহ ডিসমিস হয়।”

13. On appeal, the Court of appeal below on consideration of evidence reversed the judgment holding that the trial Court failed to decide the real controversy of the suit which is whether service of summons of the earlier title suit was suppressed or not and, as such, the decree is collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs-appellants, rather, raised the question of title, thus, committed error. The learned Single Judge without making any decision regarding the judgment of the Court of appeal below made the Rule absolute. Hence, this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal.

14. Before adverting to the contentions raised from the respective sides it will be useful to notice the relevant provisions of law i.e. Rule 17 of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure (briefly the Code) which contemplated the provisions servicing of summon affixing when the defendants are absent or refuses to sign the acknowledgement. The Rule 17 under Order V of the Code is hereby quoted below: "17. Where the defendant or his agent or such other person as aforesaid refuses to sign the acknowledgement, or where the serving officer, after using all due and reasonable diligence, cannot find the defendant, and there is no agent empowered to accept service of the summons on his behalf, nor any other person on whom service can be made, the serving officer shall affix a copy of the summons on the outer door or some other conspicuous part of the house in which the defendant ordinarily resides or carries on business or personally works for gain, and shall then return the original to the Court from which it was issued, with a report endorsed thereon or annexed thereto stating that he has so affixed the copy, the circumstances under which he did so, and the name and address of the person (if any) by whom the house was identified and in whose presence the copy was affixed."

15. The plaintiffs filed the suit not for declaration of title but declaration that ex-parte decree was collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon them. The trial Court took the view that the plaintiffs failed to establish their title, hence, suit was dismissed. The same view took the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division but Court of appeal below took the different view asserting that the real dispute in the suit is whether summons of the suit was served according to taw and ex-parte judgment is collusive and fraudulent.

16. We now turn to the vital contentions whether in a suit for declaration to set-aside the ex-parte decree Court can consider the servicing of summons or title of the plaintiffs as opined by the High Court Division.

17. It is the cardinal maxim of the law that in a judgment the Court must decide the real controversy between the parties framing issues. The learned Assistant Judge framed the following issues those are reproduced herein below. ১। মোকদ্দমাটি বর্তমান আকারে প্রকারে চলতে পারে কিনা? ২। মোকদ্দমাটি তামাদি বারিত কিনা? ৩। দেং ৪০০/৮৩ নং মোকদ্দমায় প্রদত্ত ডিক্রী রদ রহিত যোগ্য কিনা? ৪। নালিশী জমিতে বাদীপক্ষে স্বত্ব দখল আছে কিনা? ৫। বাদী প্রার্থীত প্রতিকার পেতে পারেন কিনা? ৬। বাদী আর কি প্রতিকার পেতে পারেন?

18. It appears from the judgment that the learned Assistant Judge discussed the issue Nos.3 and 4 analogously and did not opine about the issue No.3 independently. The issue No.3 is the essential issuein the suit, issue No.4 is not the proper issue in the suit. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division failed to appreciate the above failure of the Judge of the trial Court, not only so, rather, concurred with the findings and discussion of the trial Court on the issues, although the Court of appeal below clearly found that the discussion of the trial Court was erroneous, thus the Court of appeal below after proper appreciation of the materials on issues, thus, appeal was allowed. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division without rebutting finding of the Court of appeal below reversed the judgment which is not only improper, rather, erroneous, thus committed serious error in law, occasioning failure of justice.

19. In a suit for cancellation of ex-parte decree essential element is whether there was fraudulent suppression of summons. Now, the question is who will prove the service of summons in the present suit. It is found from the averment of the suit and the testimony of PW No.1, who has categorically denied the service of summons of the suit upon him and told that summons were suppressed by the plaintiffs of the earlier suit with the connivance of the process server of the Court. Upon such allegation of the PW 1 in his testimonies which are prima facie proving the case in his favour, then it is incumbent upon the defendant to prove the service of summons of the earlier suit by adducing proper witness. Because burden of proof has been shifted upon the defendant to prove that summons were duly served upon the defendant of earlier suit as per provisions of section 103 of the Evidence Act which is quoted herein below for the benefit of the discussions; "103. Burden of proof as to particular fact—The burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the Court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided by any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on any particular person."

20. The learned Assistant Judge himself opined in the judgment that there are same anomalies on serving the summons. In view of such opinion the ex-parte judgment cannot be sustained in law. The proper service of summons is a pre-requisite of sustainability of an ex-parte decree. It has held by this Division in the case of Abdur Rashed vs Abdul Barik reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162— "An ex-parte decree will be set-aside if it is found that there was no service of summons on the defendant."

21. In a suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree, in a case of service by hanging because of alleged refusal by the plaintiff appellant to receive notices, where the names and addresses of the mukabila witnesses were not noted in the service reports by the process server, it is the settled principles of law from the long line of catena, obviously process server most examine by the Court, but in the instant case the process server was not adduced to examine by the Court, even then, the trial Court found from record that there are some anomalies in the serving of the summons, such facts would lead to disbelieve the service which is devoid of the essential information as requires by law. But the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division failed to appreciate the above legal proposition. Thus, committed serious error of law point occasioning failure of justice. It is the cardinal principles of law that in a suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree determination of title is not the essential ingredient as decided by the learned Single Judge in the instant revisional case, thus acted beyond the revisional jurisdiction in making the Rule absolute setting aside well founded judgment of the Court of appeal below. Thus, committed error of law occasioning failure of justice. However, we are of the opinion that, if we grant leave to appeal then the litigation will prolong for the uncertain period, hence, we are inclined to dispose of the petition for early disposal of the suit.

22. In view of the above discussion, we find merit in this petition. Accordingly, this petition is disposed of. The judgment of the High Court Division is hereby set-aside. The trial Court is hereby directed to conclude the trial as early as possible preferably within 1(one) year from the date of receipt of this judgment positively.

End.
